text:
marta: Heads-up — after the CUDA driver 546.12 rollout to our eu-west pools we started seeing a kernel-path flip in the autotuner. Small-batch vectorized path chosen for a lot of 32/64-token requests that previously went through the hybrid-attn fastpath. Observed ~18% drop in throughput for our p99 inference jobs. KV cache hit rate unchanged.

marta: Short profiler excerpt:
```
Model: redwood/opt-6.7
Host: eu-west-gpu-3
Driver: 546.12
Batch distribution: 1-4 tokens heavy
Kernel pick: vectorized_small_batch (was hybrid_fastpath)
Throughput: 820 qps -> 670 qps
Latency p99: 110ms -> 138ms
KVcache: hitrate 0.74 -> 0.73
```

marta: tagging ops, need quick triage. rollback or force heuristic? :eyes:

sam: ack. thanks for the details. first quick check — is this across all instance types or just A100/h100 mix?

marta: mainly h100s in eu-west; a handful of a100 hosts but no regressions there.

jules: interesting — driver bump changed the kernel selection score for small seqs. i've seen autotuner weights shift when cuBLAS/cuDNN microkernels change. can you dump kernel-score telemetry for a few requests? (link to perf dashboard would help)

marta: posted full trace to perf dashboard: <https://perf.redwood.internal/trace/2250012345> — includes kernel pick history for the affected requests.

kevin: quick mitigation options:
- pin driver on affected fleet to previous stable (543.21) via rollout agent
- force kernel selector to use legacy heuristic for seq-length < 128 (config flag)
- flip autotuner to "stable" (no online re-ranking)
Any preference?

anita: rolling driver rollback has customer impact windows but is safest. forcing selector override sounds low-risk if we can target only canary pools.

marta: preference: target canary rollback first and force selector override as kill-switch. if canary rollback restores throughput we schedule fleet rollback.

ops-bot: scheduled canary patch job: rdw-rollout --group=eu-west-canary --driver=543.21 --dry-run=false (job id: rdw-20250318-89)

jules: to force selector override add this to runtime config on canaries: 
```json
{"kernel_selector_mode":"legacy_tiebreak","seq_len_threshold":128}
```
(we should not enable legacy globally).

sam: perf-run commands to collect detailed traces on canary:
```
perfctl start --trace-id=2250012345-canary --hosts=eu-west-canary --duration=10m
rdw-stats dump kernel-scores --trace=2250012345-canary > /tmp/kern-scores.log
```

marta: i'm applying the selector override to canary now. will post results in ~10m.

(10 minutes later)

marta: quick update — canary with driver 543.21 restored throughput to 825 qps. canary with driver 546.12 + selector override restored to ~810 qps (still slightly lower than pre-upgrade but within noise).

jules: that indicates driver change + new kernel ranking algorithm both contributed. rollback is stronger fix but override buys time.

kevin: suggested rollback timeline:
- immediate: keep override enabled on 546.12 fleet as kill-switch
- 1h: start rolling driver rollback for eu-west production in 10% increments, monitor p99 and kernel-pick telemetry
- 6h: finish rollback if metrics look good, otherwise pause and escalate

anita: i'm on-call and will own the rollback schedule. alert policy already added for kernel-pick entropy and throughput regressions.

marta: next steps for runtime team:
- jules: add a short-term autotuner patch to avoid re-ranking kernel choices for seq_len < 128 until we get microbenchmarks for 546.12
- kevin: prepare fleet rollback playbook + canary cutover commands (include rollback dry-run)
- sam: gather perf traces for both drivers and attach microbench results to the internal bug
- anita: execute rollback ops and monitor

jules: i'll open the internal issue with microbench numbers and suggested autotuner patch (link: <https://issues.redwood.internal/RED-8123>).

marta: thanks all. keeping selector override on for now. ping here when rollback started. :thumbsup:

kevin: rolling change note for ops runbook: 
"If driver rollback is required, use rdw-driver-rollback --fleet eu-west --target-version=543.21 --batch-size=10% --hold-on-alerts"

anita: starting step 1 (10% rollback) in 5m. will update with timestamps and graphs.

marta: appreciated. leaving this thread pinned for postmortem notes.

ops-bot: incident created RED-ENG-2250012345 (severity: P2)

marta: postmortem TODOs: add regression timeline, kernel-score change diff, autotuner config diff, decision log for rollback vs override, customer impact summary.

sam: adding perf artifacts to the postmortem now.

jules: tentative action item: add a test in our upgrade CI that runs kernel-selection microbench across driver candidates for seq_len buckets [1-32,33-128,129-512]. should catch these shifts earlier.

marta: good call. closing for now — will reopen if rollback doesn't converge.
